html:
Ayutthaya was founded in 1351 by King U Thong on an island where three rivers meet in the lower Chao Phraya valley. It was the capital of Siam for 417 years.

It absorbed Sukhothai and fought Cambodia, taking Angkor (see fall of Angkor). It grew into one of the great ports of Asia, with quarters for Chinese, Japanese, Persian, Portuguese, Dutch and French traders, and it sent rice and deer hides abroad.

Its kings built a court culture of Theravada Buddhism and Khmer-style kingship. Burmese armies took it in 1569 and destroyed it in 1767. See Wat Chaiwatthanaram and Naresuan.
